title: Nous Research Hits $1.5B Valuation, Launches Hermes Agent
summary: Nous Research raises $90M Series B at $1.5B valuation and launches Hermes Agent, bringing enterprise AI automation to business users. Full details inside.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Nous Research closed a $90 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, cementing its position in enterprise AI infrastructure.
- The company officially launched Hermes Agent, an AI agent platform designed to automate workflows for business users without coding expertise.
- Hermes Agent targets operational automation across sales, customer support, and internal processes with pre-built templates and integrations.


Nous Research confirmed it has reached a $1.5 billion valuation following a $90 million Series B funding round, according to a company announcement on October 7, 2026. Alongside the funding milestone, the AI research lab officially launched Hermes Agent, a platform designed to bring autonomous AI[automation](https://emergent.sh/glossary/what-is-automation) to business users without requiring technical expertise.


## Funding Round Details and Valuation


The Series B round positions Nous Research among the fastest-growing enterprise AI infrastructure providers. The company did not disclose lead investors or detailed allocation of the capital, but confirmed the funds will accelerate product development and expand enterprise partnerships. The $1.5 billion post-money valuation represents a significant jump from previous private funding rounds, reflecting investor confidence in the company's agent-based automation technology.


## Hermes Agent Platform Launch


Officially released on October 7, 2026, Hermes Agent targets operational teams in sales, customer support, and internal workflows. The platform offers pre-built agent templates for common business functions, including lead qualification, ticket routing, and document processing. Users can configure agents through a visual interface, eliminating the need for custom coding or machine learning expertise.


Key capabilities include:


- Multi-step[workflow](https://emergent.sh/glossary/workflow) automation across third-party integrations
- Natural language task delegation and status tracking
- Real-time decision-making based on structured and unstructured data
- Enterprise-grade security and compliance controls


The platform competes directly with established players in the[AI agents for business](https://emergent.sh/learn/best-ai-agents-for-business) category, differentiated by its focus on non-technical business users rather than developer-first environments.


## Target Market and Use Cases


Nous Research positions Hermes Agent as a solution for mid-market and enterprise organizations seeking to automate repetitive knowledge work. Early adopters have deployed the platform for customer onboarding, contract review, and internal help desk operations. The company emphasizes deployment speed, claiming most businesses can launch their first agent within hours using existing data sources and API connections.


The platform also supports[small business automation](https://emergent.sh/learn/ai-agents-for-small-business) through tiered pricing, making agent technology accessible beyond Fortune 500 buyers. This market expansion aligns with broader industry trends toward democratizing AI tooling for operational teams.


## Competitive Landscape


Hermes Agent enters a crowded market that includes OpenAI's recently announced sponsored agents, Microsoft's Copilot Studio, and specialized vertical solutions. Nous Research's differentiation lies in its combination of open-weight model flexibility and enterprise deployment infrastructure. The company has built integrations with major CRM, ticketing, and collaboration platforms, reducing onboarding friction for IT teams.


Industry observers note the timing of the launch capitalizes on increased enterprise demand for AI automation tools that deliver measurable ROI without requiring dedicated data science teams.


## What This Means


Nous Research's dual announcement signals a strategic shift from research-focused model development to commercialized agent products. The $1.5 billion valuation reflects market confidence in agent-based automation as a sustainable revenue model, while the Hermes Agent launch demonstrates the company's ability to package complex AI capabilities for mainstream business adoption. Organizations evaluating[business automation solutions](https://emergent.sh/ai-agent-builder/business-automation) now have another enterprise-grade option with proven funding and technical infrastructure backing.
